newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wafangdian B shares surge 81.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Wafangdian B shares surge 81.2 pct.

text.p: Foreign currency B shares in Wafangdian Bearing Co, which debuted on the Shenzhen stock exchange on Tuesday, surged 81.2 percent to HK$4.82 in mid-morning trade against an issue price of HK$2.66.
The shares opened at an intraday low of HK$4.05, or 52.26 percent up on the issue price.
The price quickly hit an intraday high of HK$5.53, rocketing nearly 150 percent from the issue price before profit-taking set in and trimmed some gains, traders said.

"Investor confidence was boosted by the fact that SKF bought 65 million shares at a 35 percent premium," a stock analyst with a western bank told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Sweden's AB SKF SKFRfb.ST bought 65 million B shares at HK$3.575 each to get a foothold in China's bearing market, lead domestic underwriter China Southern Securities has said.
"The company is the first B share firm to list in China this year and this helped boost sentiment," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Some analysts warned the stock was overpriced. "Investors have gone over the top," the Guotai Securities analyst said.
"The price is not reasonable and will lack support," said the western bank analyst.
The shares, issued earlier this month, gave a price/earnings ratio of 7.9 times based on 1996 net profit on a fully diluted basis, the company said in an earlier statement.
